name: Wrong Answers Only: Staff Edition
why_it_works: "Wrong answers only" is an open invitation: viewers instantly start writing their own joke, which keeps them watching and pulls them into the comments. When the most serious person on the team finally gives the real answer, the relief of the straight line makes the brand look both human and competent.

hook.pattern: Put the 'wrong answers only' prompt on screen about the one service people misunderstand, asked to your own team.
examples: Wrong answers only: what does a {{service}} actually do?
We asked our team what a {{service}} is. Wrong answers only.
Wrong answers only. Go. What happens at a {{service}}?

variables.name: wrong_answer_1
variables.description: First wrong answer: mild, almost plausible
variables.example: We ask the brakes how they're feeling

variables.name: wrong_answer_2
variables.example: We test them by yelling STOP really loud

variables.name: wrong_answer_3
variables.description: Third wrong answer: the biggest, most physical one
variables.example: Two of us lie in front of the car. Trust exercise.

variables.name: real_answer
variables.description: The true, plain-language answer in one sentence
variables.example: We measure pad thickness and check rotors and fluid in about 20 minutes

variables.name: callback_tag
variables.description: A short callback to wrong answer three, said straight

variables.name: offer
variables.description: What the viewer gets for acting

beats.on_screen_text: Wrong answers only: what does a {{service}} do?
beats.voiceover: Wrong answers only. What does a {{service}} actually do?

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 photo inside {{brand}}, a team member holding a handwritten cardboard sign reading WRONG ANSWERS ONLY, workplace softly blurred behind, bright natural light, centered medium shot
Vertical medium close-up of a smiling {{brand}} employee in uniform at their workstation, sincere expression as if giving a real answer, warm practical light, shallow depth of field
Vertical shot of a second {{brand}} employee mid-gesture, eyebrows raised, holding a tool or prop from the {{service}} like a microphone, playful energy, same location, eye-level framing

beats.purpose: peak: wrong answer three, most absurd

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 clip, two {{brand}} employees acting out an absurd, harmless version of the {{service}} with exaggerated seriousness, slow push-in, bright workplace light, safe and clearly staged

beats.purpose: turn: the straight answer from the most serious person

visual.prompt: Vertical medium shot, the owner of {{brand}} walks into frame behind the team, unimpressed, then turns to camera and calmly explains, clean professional light, team frozen mid-joke in the background

cta: Drop your wrong answer in the comments, then book the right one: {{offer}}.

craft.technique: Rule of three escalation with a straight-man turn
craft.notes: Setup: the 'wrong answers only' prompt and three answers that climb from mild to silly to absurd (rule of three, the third is the biggest and most physical). Turn: the most serious person on the team delivers the real answer completely straight; the comedy is the tonal whiplash. Tag: the last line calls back to wrong answer three (the callback_tag, e.g. 'No trust exercises.') so the joke pays off twice. Timing: cut each wrong answer the instant the line ends, no reaction shots, so the rhythm speeds up; then hold a half-second of silence on the owner's unimpressed face before they speak. That pause is the laugh.

do_not: Make any wrong answer sound plausible enough to be taken as real advice
Let a wrong answer mock customers, their cars, teeth, or claims; the joke is the staff being goofy
Use more than three wrong answers; a fourth kills the rhythm
Bury the real answer in jargon; it must be one clear sentence
compliance: Law firms: the real answer must be general information, not legal advice; no outcome or settlement guarantees; label as attorney advertising where your state bar requires
Dental: the real answer must be accurate and general; do not promise 'painless' or specific results; any staff shown performing care must be licensed for it
Insurance: do not imply any coverage, price or claim outcome; add 'coverage varies by policy and state' to the caption
Wrong answers must never depict an unsafe act a viewer could copy (for auto: no one under or in front of a vehicle in the final render)
